batch: P7 Sprint 2 (T1+T2+T3 CRUD + T5 aggregate/list + G-08 OpenAPI baseline)
scope: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py (8 new endpoints), pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py (9 Pydantic schemas), pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py (T5 service), pcs-backend/app/models/util.py (5 new ORM)

summary.verdict: ACCEPTABLE — no auth bypass, no SQLi, no secrets. IDOR and integrity-override are pre-existing codebase patterns; not blockers for this batch.

findings.title: IDOR — project_id not validated against user ownership
evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:411-430 list_power_items — accepts project_id UUID Query without ownership check
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:476-495 list_fuel_gas — same pattern
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:542-561 list_heat_exchange — same pattern
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:594-621 list_energy_summary — same pattern
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:380-408 create_power_item — body.project_id not bound to user.workspace
No UserProject/WorkspaceMember model exists in pcs-backend/app/models/ (grep returns empty)
current_actor (config.py:441-469) decodes JWT to _Actor but does not load project memberships
require_roles checks role string only — DESIGNER can pass for any project_id
findings.description: All 8 new endpoints accept arbitrary project_id/workspace_id from caller and skip any per-user project authorization check. A DESIGNER with a valid JWT can read or write any project's utility data by guessing or enumerating project UUIDs. require_roles gates role (DESIGNER/PROCESS_CONTROLLER/SYSTEM_ADMIN) but not project scope. Impact: cross-tenant data exposure and tampering within the lowest privileged role. Pre-existing across the whole PCS backend (no ownership table exists), not introduced by this batch.
findings.exploit_path: Attacker authenticates as DESIGNER, calls GET /api/v1/util/power-items?project_id=<victim-uuid>. require_roles passes. List returns victim's equipment_tag list. POST with attacker-chosen consumption values writes to victim's project.
findings.remediation: Add UserProject membership table; have current_actor load allowed project_ids; reject queries where requested project_id is not in actor's allowed set. Alternatively, derive project_id from a workspace_id the user already owns and reject mismatch.
findings.rationale: Pattern-level architectural gap, not introduced by Sprint 2. Not a release blocker for T1-T5 endpoints because Sprint 1 endpoints in the same file already expose the same behavior — fixing this in isolation would inconsistently protect some endpoints and not others.

findings.title: annual_consumption override bypasses derived formula (T1/T2/T3 integrity)
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py:115-117 annual_consumption_kwh: float | None = Field(None, ge=0) — only constraint is non-negative
pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py:157-159 annual_consumption_nm3: float | None = Field(None, ge=0)
pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py:206-208 annual_consumption_t: float | None = Field(None, ge=0)
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:389-393 — if user supplies annual_kwh, the derived formula is skipped entirely
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:452-456 — same for fuel_gas
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:517-521 — same for heat_exchange
No reconciliation check between user-supplied value and derived formula
Service downstream: utility_energy_summary_service aggregates these values into project-level TOE / 标煤 reports (T5)
findings.description: When the caller supplies annual_consumption_kwh (or _nm3, _t), the API layer accepts the value verbatim without comparing against the derived formula (motor_power × hours × load_factor, etc.). A DESIGNER can submit annual_consumption_kwh=1e15 for a 15 kW motor — well above any physically plausible value — and the record is persisted. Downstream, utility_energy_summary_service aggregates these into project-level TOE/standard_coal totals; an inflated value contaminates the regulatory-energy report. Not a confidentiality breach (no secrets), but data-integrity impact on regulatory submissions (折标煤).
findings.exploit_path: Attacker calls POST /api/v1/util/power-items with motor_power_kw=1, operating_hours_per_year=1, load_factor=0.01 (so derived ≈ 0.01 kWh) but annual_consumption_kwh=1e9. Server persists 1e9. Subsequent T5 aggregate produces inflated TOE.
findings.remediation: Option A: reject the override field entirely and always derive server-side. Option B: accept override only if |override - derived| / derived <= tolerance_pct (e.g. 5%). Option C: store both `derived` and `client_supplied` and require explicit flag + justification when they differ.
findings.rationale: Data integrity, not auth bypass. Pattern matches Sprint 1 util_results endpoints which accept arbitrary consumption_json from caller, so consistent with existing posture. Worth fixing but not a security blocker for this batch.

findings.title: Unconstrained string fields — source / fuel_type / temperature_class / operating_phase
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py:118-120 source: str | None = Field('MANUAL', max_length=32)
pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py:146 fuel_type: str = Field('NATURAL_GAS', max_length=32)
pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py:151-153 operating_phase: str = Field(..., max_length=16)
pcs-backend/app/schemas/util.py:199-201 temperature_class: str = Field(..., max_length=16)
DB column source has COMMENT listing enum PMS/MANUAL/CALC but no CHECK constraint enforces it
fuel_type column comment lists NATURAL_GAS/REFINERY_GAS/LPG/LNG/OTHERS but no CHECK
findings.description: String fields intended as enum-like are typed as plain `str` with only max_length constraint. Caller can supply arbitrary values (e.g., source='XSS_PAYLOAD_HERE', temperature_class='NOT_A_REAL_CLASS'). Pydantic does not validate against the documented enum. Risk is data quality, not security — strings are not rendered as HTML and are not used in SQL literals (all queries are parameterized).
findings.exploit_path: Attacker submits source='<script>alert(1)</script>'. Server stores as-is. If a future frontend renders this field without escaping, XSS occurs. Currently no XSS sink in batch.
findings.remediation: Use Literal['PMS','MANUAL','CALC'] or Pydantic Enum. Add CHECK constraints at DB layer.
findings.rationale: Advisory; no current exploit path. Pattern inherited from Sprint 1 util_results.source (also unconstrained).

findings.title: JWT role default permissive (DESIGNER) — token without role claim defaults to lowest privilege
evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/config.py:460 role = payload.get('role', 'DESIGNER') — missing role defaults to DESIGNER
This is the SAME pattern used by all util endpoints via require_roles
findings.description: current_actor (Sprint 1) defaults `role` to 'DESIGNER' when JWT omits the claim. Since DESIGNER is the lowest privilege role in this batch's require_roles call, an attacker who can mint a token without the `role` claim still passes auth and gets minimum access. Direction is safe (no privilege escalation), but it means the ACL check is only as strong as the JWT issuer. Pre-existing across all PCS endpoints.
findings.exploit_path: None directly — missing role claim yields lowest privilege. Not a vulnerability in this batch.
findings.rationale: Pre-existing across all PCS API. Direction is safe (lowest default). Out of scope for batch fix.

findings.title: XLS_REFERENCE tolerance_status leak surface — verified safe
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:194 xls_reference parameter — service-level only
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/util.py:569-591 aggregate_energy_summary — body schema UtilEnergySummaryAggregateRequest has NO source/xls_reference field
Source is hardcoded to 'CALCULATION' at API layer
Tolerance status returned is enum string 'OK'/'EXCEEDED'/'NA' — no underlying reference value exposed
tolerance_pct is a float ratio, no raw XLS value leaked
findings.description: Concern was that the new API endpoints might expose XLS_REFERENCE-derived tolerance data or allow client to inject XLS_REFERENCE as source. Verified: aggregate_energy_summary does not accept source override (always CALCULATION), and tolerance_pct is just a ratio. No data leak.
findings.remediation: None needed. Continue to keep xls_reference service-internal.
findings.rationale: Clean — explicit verification done. Listed for completeness of the checklist.

checked_negatives: SQL injection — all queries use SQLAlchemy bound parameters (where(Project.id == x)); no f-strings, .format(), or string concatenation in any query
SQL injection via project_id/equipment_tag — both UUID and str types are parameterized; FastAPI validates UUID format before query
Missing auth — every endpoint has current_actor dependency; missing/invalid JWT → 401
Missing ACL — all 8 endpoints verified to call require_roles(user, 'DESIGNER', 'PROCESS_CONTROLLER', 'SYSTEM_ADMIN')
Hardcoded secrets — no API keys, passwords, or tokens in new code
Command injection — no os.system, subprocess, eval, exec calls
SSRF/path traversal — endpoints do not fetch URLs or read filesystem paths
Mass assignment — Pydantic models explicitly enumerate fields; no **kwargs or attribute assignment from raw dict
Float NaN/Inf — Pydantic Field(gt=0, le=8760) rejects NaN (NaN>0 == False) and Inf (Inf<=8760 == False); 422 returned
Sensitive logging — no print() or logger.info/calls in new endpoints that emit project_id, equipment_tag, or tokens
CSRF — Bearer token in Authorization header; browsers cannot set this cross-origin without explicit CORS allowlist
Unbounded queries — list endpoints have limit ge=1 le=500 and offset ge=0; prevent DoS via giant result sets
equipment_tag length DoS — bounded by String(64) in DB and max_length=64 in Pydantic
source field length DoS — bounded max_length=32 in Pydantic and String(32) in DB
Path param enumeration — all {id} path params are uuid.UUID (no integer enumeration)
Raw SQL — no execute(text(...)) calls; all queries go through select() ORM API

covered: test_util_sprint2.py covers 201/200 happy paths for T1 + T5 with DESIGNER token
Annual_consumption derivation path tested (line 99 omits annual_consumption_kwh)
gaps: No test for ACL denial (non-DESIGNER role → 403)
No test for annual_consumption override with implausibly large value (SEC-P7S2-002 exploit path)
No test for cross-project access by DESIGNER (SEC-P7S2-001 exploit path)
No test for source field XSS-style payload (SEC-P7S2-003)

recommendations: P2 SEC-P7S2-001: address IDOR via project membership table in a dedicated batch (cross-cutting)
P2 SEC-P7S2-002: decide on annual_consumption override policy (reject, tolerance-check, or audit-log)
ship_decision: APPROVE-with-followup — no P0/P1. Two P2 (one pre-existing, one new) registered for next batch.
open_questions: Is there a documented product decision on whether DESIGNER should be able to access any project_id, or only assigned projects? If the latter, SEC-P7S2-001 becomes a P1.

Is annual_consumption_kwh override (T1/T2/T3) intentional to support CALC-source corrections (e.g., PMS-derived values that differ from formula)? If yes, add a tolerance check + audit log; if no, remove the field.
Will frontend render source / equipment_tag / fuel_type strings directly? If yes, escape on output (already FastAPI JSON default); if rendered in HTML, ensure template autoescape.
